faq.answer: If return is impractical (perishable/cultural reasons), accept and transfer to HR for donation or shared distribution.
Must be declared; if third party attends with business discussion, treat as entertainment rather than gift.

rules.source_quote: Client entertainment per-person caps are governed by TEP-002 §4.
Client entertainment requires one or more external attendees documented on the receipt.
Cash and cash equivalents (including gift cards exceeding $25) may never be accepted.
Non-cash gifts may be accepted up to $50 per gift and $200 cumulatively per source per calendar year.
Gifts above $50 must be declined/returned; if return impractical, hand over to HR for donation/shared distribution.
Nominal promotional items (e.g., branded pens/notepads/water) are not considered gifts under this policy.
Client gifts are permitted up to $100 per recipient per calendar year.
Gifts to government/public-sector/state-owned enterprise representatives are prohibited unless General Counsel written approval exists.
Cash and cash-equivalent gifts to clients are prohibited under all circumstances.
Entertainment including spouses/family members requires VP-level approval and clear business rationale.
Tickets from third parties must be declared if face value exceeds $50.
